candidate.answerReason: One suspension identifies only a line containing the center of gravity. Two suitably chosen suspensions give distinct lines through it, whose unique intersection determines its position. The minimum is 2.

methods.label: Intersect suspension lines
methods.explanation: Two nonparallel lines intersect at one point. Suspending the plate 2 times produces two lines, and their intersection is the center of gravity.
methods.levelReason: Uses the Grade 8 suspension method and elementary facts about coplanar lines.

candidate.annotationRationale: Locating the center of gravity by suspension directly matches cnm_119. The planar parallel-line definition in cnm_067 supports intersection of nonparallel lines, while the two-point line uniqueness fact in cnm_054 supports uniqueness of that intersection. The retained prose is the supplied machine translation of AI-generated text, not teacher reviewed.
limitations: The suspensions must be chosen to give distinct marked lines on the plate. Coincident lines do not locate a unique point.
candidate.changeReason: The existing nonparallel-line condition correctly gives a unique intersection for two suitably chosen suspensions. One line alone is insufficient, so the minimum remains 2 with the recorded line-choice qualification.
